views.name: crime_enforcement_equity
views.comment: Correlates FBI CDE monthly offense and clearance rates — averaged across each year's reported months, NOT summed to a true annual rate (see cde_offenses.offense_rate for why AVG understates the annual figure) — with police employment and an offense-rate-per-officer ratio, by state, year, and offense_code. One row per state + year + offense_code.
views.sql:
SELECT
  o.state_abbr,
  gs.state_name,
  gs.state_fips,
  o.year,
  o.offense_code,
  AVG(o.offense_rate)                                  AS avg_monthly_offense_rate,
  AVG(o.clearance_rate)                                AS avg_monthly_clearance_rate,
  pe.officers_per_1000,
  pe.male_officers + pe.female_officers                AS total_officers,
  CASE
    WHEN pe.officers_per_1000 IS NOT NULL
      AND pe.officers_per_1000 > 0
    THEN AVG(o.offense_rate) / pe.officers_per_1000
    ELSE NULL
  END                                                  AS offense_rate_per_officer
FROM cde_offenses o LEFT JOIN cde_police_employment pe
  ON o.state_abbr = pe.state_abbr AND o.year = pe.year
LEFT JOIN "geo"."states" gs ON o.state_abbr = gs.state_abbr GROUP BY o.state_abbr, gs.state_name, gs.state_fips, o.year, o.offense_code,
         pe.officers_per_1000, pe.male_officers, pe.female_officers

partitionedTables.name: bjs_ncvs_personal_pop
partitionedTables.comment: Bureau of Justice Statistics NCVS personal population data. Demographic information for all survey respondents regardless of victimization status. Includes age, sex, race, Hispanic origin, marital status, education, income. Same 2010-onward coverage and ~2-year publish lag as bjs_ncvs_personal. Used as denominator for computing victimization rates from bjs_ncvs_personal.

partitionedTables.name: bjs_ncvs_household
partitionedTables.comment: Bureau of Justice Statistics NCVS household victimization microdata, one row per household-level victimization incident, coded by newcrime/newoff crime and offense type codes. Includes police notification status, region/MSA, household income bracket, and household victimization weight (wgtviccy). Same 2010-onward coverage and ~2-year publish lag as bjs_ncvs_personal. Cross-references bjs_ncvs_household_pop as the denominator for household victimization rates.

operands.comment: Comprehensive U.S. crime and public safety data from FBI Crime Data Explorer (CDE) and Bureau of Justice Statistics (BJS). CDE tables cover law enforcement agencies, summarized offense rates, agency-level offenses, arrests, supplementary homicide reports (SHR), police employment, hate crimes, use of force, LEOKA (officers killed/assaulted), cargo theft, human trafficking, agency participation rates, and estimated crime counts. BJS tables cover NIBRS national crime estimates, NCVS personal and household victimization, and NCVS population data. All state-level tables join with geo.states via state_abbr.
